For you I'd trigger it on each new HubSpot form submission and write the score and summary to custom properties. requirements.point: answers from policy PDFs with sources
requirements.quote: answer employee questions from our 300 policy PDFs
It must say when it doesn't know.

job04_policy_rag.txt.opening_detail: answer employee questions from our 300 policy PDFs
job04_policy_rag.txt.proposal: Answering employee questions from your 300 policy PDFs, always with the source, is close to what I built for security questionnaires (P2): it drafts answers from a company's own documents, cites a source for every answer and checks numbers and claims in code, so unsupported answers are flagged instead of shown. For you I'd add a simple chat page on AWS and an "I don't know" path when no policy covers the question. First step: share a few sample PDFs and real questions, and I'll show you answers with their citations.
answers: Every answer must cite the passage it came from, and code checks that numbers and claims appear in the cited text; if nothing supports an answer, it says it doesn't know.
For a few hundred PDFs, keyword search plus a small embedding index in Postgres (pgvector) is enough and cheap to run on AWS; a dedicated vector database only pays off for a much larger collection.

requirements.quote: extract vendor, date, line items and totals from PDF invoices

job08_invoice_pdf.txt.opening_detail: extract vendor, date, line items and totals from PDF invoices
job08_invoice_pdf.txt.proposal: To extract vendor, date, line items and totals from PDF invoices and create bills in QuickBooks Online, I'd reuse the approach of my wholesale order agent (P3): it turns emailed PDF and Excel purchase orders into Shopify draft orders and checks every price and total in code. For your invoices the same checks apply (line totals must add up, the vendor must exist) before anything reaches QuickBooks, and anything uncertain goes to your bookkeeper's review list. First step: a handful of sample invoices so I can show you the extracted fields side by side.
answers: Not in a delivered project yet. My order agent (P3) posts to the Shopify Admin API the same way, and QuickBooks Online's API for bills follows a similar pattern.
